correctness.rationale: The ordered per-point energy has one within-lattice sum and one cross-coset sum (the two cross orientations agree by reflection and are averaged over the two representatives). Gaussian summability justifies the thermodynamic limit: truncate separations first, use vanishing boundary fraction, then control the summable tails. The cross term is F_A(v_a)F_B(v_b); evenness kills the mixed derivative. Poisson summation and two log derivatives of the theta product give K_T=F_T''(0)/F_T(0)=(8π²/T²) Σ_{j≥1}q^(2j−1)/(1−q^(2j−1))², q=exp(−π²/(αT²)). The derivatives converge locally uniformly, the curvatures are positive, and each product factor minimizes strictly at the half-cell phase modulo T. With x=π²/(αT²), K_T/T² is a positive common factor times a sum of [x/sinh((2j−1)x/2)]². Each summand decreases strictly with x, since u cosh(u)−sinh(u)>0 for u>0, giving λ_A/λ_B> A²/B²=3. In real space the two nearest terms give K_T=α²T²−2α+O(α² exp(−2αT²)); dividing at A²=3B² gives 3+4/(αB²)+O(α⁻²), including sharpness. The first term in the dual sum gives the stated broad-Gaussian exponential and prefactor 1/3. The mixture inequality follows by adding diagonal Hessians with positive weights.
residual_risks: The energy identity is for distinct cosets; its continuation at a coset coincidence is not the single-coset energy.
Only fixed-lattice relative displacements and finite positive mixtures are assessed.
